messages:
alex: Quick note: discovered sampleapp ignores REDWOOD_API_KEY if RW_LEGACY_KEY present. Broke our rotate-key flow in staging.

maya: Oof, which sampleapp?

alex: quickstart-python. Repro: set both envs, rotate REDWOOD_API_KEY, process keeps using RW_LEGACY_KEY.

jin: That sounds like a precedence bug in the vendored client. We added RW_LEGACY_KEY years ago for transition and probably never removed it.

alex: Minimal repro: 
```bash
export RW_LEGACY_KEY=old
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=new
python demo.py  # still auths with old
```

maya: Short fix: update rotate helper to write RW_LEGACY_KEY when rotating and emit a log that both were updated. Longer: SDK should prefer REDWOOD_API_KEY and emit deprecation warning if legacy env present.

jin: I'll file a tiny patch in sdk-python to warn and flip precedence. Also add a note in onboarding: "Keep single secret in CI".

ops-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/77 labels: sdk,auth,rotation

alex: Also flag runtime: streams that re-use token objects mid-stream may not pick up new envs after rotation. We should document recommended client behavior: re-auth on reconnect only.

maya: Filed follow-up for eng-runtime about streaming re-auth behavior.

jin: Plan: 1) emergency rotate-helper update to write legacy env; 2) SDK patch for deprecation + precedence; 3) docs blurb; 4) runtime follow-up.

alex: Thanks — I'll add a tiny e2e in sampleapps to catch this next time. :thumbsup:
